## Correction to this card's own citation, plus a second defect on the same line

Filed by me; correcting it is mine. Two things, both measured on `origin/main` today, `2026-09-14T13:0xZ`.

### 1. The line number in this card has drifted — `:288` is now `:287`

This card's body cites **`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:288`** twice. At `origin/main` today the instruction is at **`:287`**:

```
287| - 认领写 `Clause-②: yes` ⇒ 开 PR 同笔挂 `needs:contract-review`,报告附 `--pair N` 退出码。
288| - 触 `skills/**`(对外发布的技能包)的 diff:PR 正文报两个读数,并默认拒绝小功能大扩写。
```

⇒ `:288` now points at an unrelated line about `skills/**` diffs. ⭐ **The finding itself is unaffected** — the instruction exists, at `:287`, and still orders the dev seat to hang a label the container forbids it to hang. Only the pointer is wrong.

⚠️ Worth stating plainly because this card is about instruction accuracy: **I cited a bare line number with no sha, which is not a citation.** Whether `:288` was right when filed and drifted, or was wrong from the start, cannot now be recovered from the card — and that unrecoverability is the whole defect. ⭐ The durable form is to cite by **content** (the line's text, or the rule it states) and give a sha when a number is used at all. Whoever takes this card should re-derive the line rather than trusting either number.

### 2. The same line carries a SECOND instruction defect: `--pair N` is ambiguous, and the ambiguity is live

`:287` ends *"报告附 `--pair N` 退出码"*. The `N` is unbound. `--pair` takes a **PR** number, but the sentence's subject up to that point is the **card** — so the nearest referent is the wrong one.

Measured against the script's own source:

- `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs:11` — `node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 13910 # ONE PR: a pre-arm predicate`
- `:498` — *"`--pair` is a PREDICATE about the pair named on the command line"*

Passing a card number makes the pair unformable and the script refuses with **exit 2**: *"⛔ Not a clearance — the pair could not be formed, so nothing about it was judged."* ⭐ **That exit 2 is NOT MEASURED — never a pass and never a red.** A seat that captures the exit code as a gate verdict reads a refusal as a failing gate.

**The correct spelling already exists in exactly one governed place**, which is what makes the other two a defect rather than a convention:

| file | spelling | ambiguous? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md:42` | `--pair PR-NUMBER` | ✅ no |
| `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:645` | `--pair N` | ⛔ yes |
| `.claude/agents/os-dev.md:287` | `--pair N` | ⛔ yes |

⇒ the fix is mechanical: make `PR-NUMBER` the only spelling.

### Why both belong on this card rather than a new one

Same file, same line, same class — **an instruction that cannot be followed correctly returns the same signal as one that was.** This card already names that class for the label write; the `--pair` ambiguity is the second instance on the identical line.

**Provenance, disclosed:** I shipped `--pair <card>` into two live dispatch orders today and corrected them in flight. It was caught because a dev ran my version, got the refusal, **read what the script actually said instead of substituting quietly, and reported it** — the third time today an instruction defect of mine was caught by an agent verifying rather than complying. ⭐ The suggested direction from that dev is worth recording: mechanise the two that are mechanisable — a console-selection reader that refuses to report a number unless its self-test leg fired, and a clause-2 wrapper that names the argument it expects — rather than fixing the three instances.

⛔ Not graded and not routed by me; this card is `finding` and its triage is objectstack's.

Re-read on `b3b43b6`: os-dev.md :287 and SKILL.md :646 spell `--pair N`; contract-review.md :42 spells `--pair PR-NUMBER`. `finding` dropped; **`pm:queue` · Bug · `priority:p2`**. Direction (seat reading, veto window): (A) the carrier is the PM seat's to hang — at the claim (card side) and when the PR appears (PR side), which is what every seat already does; the dev reports the label state it observed and never blocks on a label write; `--pair PR-NUMBER` becomes the only spelling in all three files; #18156's ② (the check runs from the objectstack checkout with `PM_SWEEP_REPO=objectstack-ai/objectui`) lands as the same line's remedy text. (B) granting the dev container the label write is a permissions widening on the manual floor — ⛔ not this card; the maintainer may take it instead in the veto window. `Clause-②: no`. Serial: os-dev.md is free; SKILL.md :646 is on the SKILL.md chain behind #17374 (second half) and #17497 — the dispatch decides whether the os-dev.md half goes first as its own PR. #18156 (the objectui spec seat's twin: the dispatch order's label red line vs the standing clause, plus the `--pair` evidence only the seat can produce) is CLOSED as a duplicate of this card in the same act; its ② fact is carried here. Governed rules layer ⇒ four-piece and an authorized approval; build tier per `--tier` (os-dev.md ⇒ the contract-review tier, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`).
